senses.def: a room where scientific experiments are done (short for laboratory)
ex: The students worked in the lab.
The results came back from the lab.

senses.def: a piece of paper or cloth fixed to something that gives information about it
ex: Read the label on the bottle.
The label says the shirt is cotton.

senses.def: a room or building with equipment for scientific work
ex: The laboratory tested the water.
She works in a research laboratory.

senses.def: the state of not having enough of something
ex: There is a lack of water in the village.
His lack of experience was a problem.

senses.def: to not have something, or not have enough of it
ex: She lacks confidence.
The room lacks light.

mistake.note: 'Lack' as a verb takes a direct object with no preposition.

senses.def: a tool with steps used to climb up or down
ex: He climbed the ladder to fix the roof.
Hold the ladder for me.

senses.def: a polite word for a woman
ex: That lady is waiting for the bus.
Good evening, ladies and gentlemen.

senses.def: a large area of water with land all around it
ex: We swam in the lake.
The lake is very deep.

senses.def: a young sheep
ex: The lamb stayed close to its mother.

senses.def: meat from a young sheep
ex: We had roast lamb for dinner.

senses.def: weak and not good enough to convince people
ex: He gave a lame excuse for being late.
The joke was a bit lame.

senses.def: unable to walk properly because of an injured leg (old-fashioned)
ex: The horse went lame.

senses.def: to express sadness or regret about something
ex: She lamented the loss of her youth.
People lament the disappearance of small shops.

senses.def: a long weapon with a sharp point, used in the past by soldiers on horses
ex: The knight carried a lance.

senses.def: to arrive on the ground after being in the air
ex: The plane lands at six o'clock.
The bird landed on the roof.

senses.def: the solid part of the earth's surface, not the sea
ex: After days at sea, they saw land.
The farmer owns a lot of land.

senses.def: a country or area
ex: He travelled to a distant land.

senses.def: the act of an aircraft coming down onto the ground
ex: The pilot made a smooth landing.
We felt a bump on landing.

senses.def: the flat area at the top of a set of stairs
ex: She waited on the landing.

senses.def: a woman who owns a house or flat and rents it to others
ex: The landlady asked us to pay the rent.
Our landlady is very friendly.

senses.def: a man who owns a house or flat and rents it to others
ex: The landlord is raising the rent.
We called our landlord about the leak.

senses.def: a narrow road, especially in the countryside
ex: We walked down a quiet country lane.

senses.def: one of the parts of a road or track marked for one line of traffic
ex: He moved into the left lane.
She swam in lane three.

senses.def: the flat area formed by your thighs when you sit down
ex: The cat sat on my lap.

senses.def: one complete circuit of a track in a race
ex: He ran ten laps around the track.

senses.def: a short time when you fail to do something well
ex: She had a lapse of memory.
A lapse in concentration caused the accident.

senses.def: to end because you did not renew it
ex: My membership lapsed last month.

senses.def: a small computer that you can carry and use anywhere
ex: She works on her laptop at the café.
He packed his laptop in his bag.

senses.def: a small brown bird that sings beautifully
ex: We heard a lark singing over the field.

senses.def: something done for fun (informal)
ex: They climbed the wall just for a lark.

senses.def: an illness in which the throat becomes sore and it is hard to speak
ex: He had laryngitis and could hardly speak.

senses.def: a strong narrow beam of light used for cutting, surgery and many other purposes
ex: The doctor used a laser to treat his eyes.
The show had colourful laser lights.

senses.def: most recent, or coming just before now
ex: I saw him last week.
What did you do last night?

senses.def: coming at the end
ex: This is the last bus.

senses.def: the person or thing that comes at the end
ex: He was the last to arrive.
The last of the guests left at midnight.

senses.def: most recently, or after all others
ex: When did you last see her?
She came last in the race.

senses.def: to continue for a period of time
ex: The film lasts two hours.
The good weather didn't last.

mistake.wrong: I travelled last year to Spain in the last week.
mistake.right: I travelled to Spain last week.
mistake.note: Do not use 'the' before 'last' when it means 'the most recent' (last week, not the last week).

senses.def: done at the latest possible time before an event
ex: We booked a last-minute holiday.
She made a last-minute change to the plan.

senses.def: arriving or happening after the expected or usual time
ex: I'm sorry I'm late.
The train was late.

senses.def: near the end of a period of time
ex: We met in late summer.

senses.def: after the expected or usual time
ex: He came home late.
I woke up late today.

mistake.note: 'Late' is also an adverb; 'lately' means 'recently'.

senses.def: in the recent past
ex: I haven't seen him lately.
Have you been busy lately?

senses.def: existing but not yet active or noticeable
ex: She has a latent talent for music.
The disease can remain latent for years.

senses.def: at a time after now or after the time mentioned
ex: See you later!
Two years later, they moved to Dubai.

senses.def: coming after something else in time
ex: We will discuss it at a later date.
The later chapters are more difficult.

senses.def: the most recent or newest
ex: Have you seen their latest film?
This is the latest phone.

senses.def: the sound or act of laughing
ex: The room was full of laughter.
We heard laughter from the garden.

senses.def: to start something new, such as a product or plan
ex: The company launched a new phone.
They launched a campaign to save water.

senses.def: to send a rocket or missile into the air
ex: Scientists launched a satellite.

senses.def: the time when a new product or project is introduced
ex: The launch of the app is next week.

senses.def: clothes and other things that need to be washed or have just been washed
ex: I do the laundry on Sundays.
She hung the laundry outside.

senses.def: hot liquid rock that comes out of a volcano
ex: Lava flowed down the mountain.

senses.def: a toilet, or a room with a toilet (formal or old-fashioned)
ex: The lavatory is at the end of the corridor.

senses.def: a rule made by a government that people must obey
ex: It is against the law to steal.
The new law bans smoking.

senses.def: the whole system of rules in a country
ex: She studies law at university.

senses.def: an area of short grass in a garden or park
ex: He mows the lawn every week.
The children played on the lawn.

senses.def: a case in a court of law brought by one person or group against another
ex: She filed a lawsuit against the company.
The lawsuit lasted three years.

senses.def: a person whose job is to give legal advice and help people in court
ex: He hired a lawyer to help him.
My sister is a lawyer.

senses.def: to put something carefully in a flat position
ex: She laid the baby on the bed.
Lay the book on the table.

senses.def: to produce an egg
ex: The hen lays an egg every day.

mistake.wrong: I am going to lay on the sofa.
mistake.right: I am going to lie on the sofa.
mistake.note: 'Lay' needs an object (lay something down); use 'lie' when you rest yourself.

senses.def: a flat covering or thickness of something over a surface or between others
ex: A thin layer of snow covered the ground.
The cake has three layers.

senses.def: the position in front of others in a race or competition
ex: She is in the lead.
Our team took the lead in the second half.

senses.def: most important, in a role or group
ex: She is the lead singer.
He plays the lead role in the film.

senses.def: to go in front to show others the way
ex: She led us to the hotel.
This path leads to the beach.

senses.def: to be in charge of a group or an activity
ex: He leads a team of ten people.

senses.def: the position or skill of being in charge of a group
ex: The team needs strong leadership.
She showed good leadership.

senses.def: most important or best in a particular area
ex: She is a leading expert on climate change.
It's the country's leading bank.

senses.def: a group of sports teams that play against each other
ex: Our team won the league.
He plays in a local football league.

senses.def: a hole or crack through which liquid or gas escapes
ex: There's a leak in the roof.
They found a gas leak.

senses.def: the act of secretly telling information to the public
ex: The newspaper printed a leak from the meeting.

senses.def: to let liquid or gas escape through a hole, or to escape that way
ex: The pipe is leaking.
Water leaked through the ceiling.

senses.def: to secretly give information to the public
ex: Someone leaked the news to the press.

senses.def: thin and healthy-looking, with no extra fat
ex: He has a lean body.
She prefers lean meat.

senses.def: to bend your body in a direction, or to rest against something
ex: She leaned over the table.
He leaned against the wall.

senses.def: to jump high or a long way
ex: The cat leaped onto the wall.
He leaped out of bed.

senses.def: a big jump, or a sudden large change
ex: The horse took a great leap.
The new phone is a leap forward in technology.

senses.def: the process of getting knowledge or skill
ex: Learning a language takes time.
She loves online learning.

senses.def: a legal agreement to rent a building or land for a period of time
ex: They signed a two-year lease on the flat.
The lease ends in June.

senses.def: a long thin strap fixed to a dog's collar to control it
ex: Dogs must be kept on a leash in the park.
He took the dog off its leash.

senses.def: the smallest amount of something
ex: She has the least money of all of us.
I have the least time.

senses.def: to the smallest degree
ex: This is the least expensive hotel.
I like him least of all.

senses.def: the smallest amount or number
ex: That's the least I can do.
It costs at least ten pounds.

senses.def: to go away from a place or person
ex: The bus leaves at nine.
She left the room.

senses.def: to put something somewhere and not take it with you
ex: I left my phone at home.
Leave the door open.

senses.def: time that you are allowed to be away from work
ex: She is on sick leave.
He took a week's leave.

mistake.wrong: I left from the house at eight.
mistake.right: I left the house at eight.
mistake.note: 'Leave' takes a direct object, so do not add 'from' before the place you leave.

senses.def: a talk on a subject given to a group, especially at a university
ex: The professor gave a lecture on history.
I have a lecture at ten.

senses.def: on or towards the side of the body that is opposite the right
ex: Raise your left hand.
The shop is on the left side.

senses.def: towards the left side
ex: Turn left at the traffic lights.

senses.def: the left side or direction
ex: Look to the left.
The bank is on your left.

senses.def: something that remains from the past or from a person who has died
ex: The artist left a rich legacy.
The war's legacy is still felt today.

senses.def: allowed by the law
ex: It is legal to drive at 18.
The contract is legal.

senses.def: relating to the law
ex: She needs legal advice.

senses.def: in a way that is allowed or required by the law
ex: You are legally required to wear a seat belt.
They are legally married.

senses.def: a very old story that may not be true
ex: According to legend, a giant lived here.
The legend of King Arthur is famous.

senses.def: a very famous person who is admired
ex: He is a football legend.

senses.def: very famous and admired for a long time
ex: The legendary singer retired last year.
His kindness is legendary.

senses.def: existing in legends
ex: The dragon is a legendary creature.

senses.def: a large group of soldiers in the ancient Roman army
ex: The Roman legion marched across the river.

senses.def: a very large number of people
ex: Legions of fans waited outside.

senses.def: a law or set of laws made by a government
ex: New legislation will protect the environment.
The legislation was passed last year.

senses.def: allowed by law or accepted as fair and reasonable
ex: It is a legitimate business.
She has a legitimate reason for being late.

senses.def: the measurement of how long something is
ex: The room is five metres in length.
What is the length of the river?

senses.def: the amount of time that something lasts
ex: The length of the film is two hours.

senses.def: a large wild cat with yellow fur and dark spots
ex: A leopard climbed up the tree.
The leopard hunts at night.

senses.def: to a smaller degree
ex: I go out less now.
This one is less expensive.

senses.def: a smaller amount of something
ex: I'd like less sugar, please.
We have less time than before.

senses.def: a smaller amount
ex: I earn less than my brother.
Less is more.

mistake.note: Use 'fewer' with countable nouns and 'less' with uncountable nouns.

senses.def: in order to avoid something bad happening (formal)
ex: She hid the letter lest he should see it.
Write it down lest you forget.

senses.def: to allow someone to do something
ex: My parents let me stay out late.
Let me help you.

senses.def: used in 'let's' to suggest doing something together
ex: Let's go to the beach.

mistake.wrong: My teacher let us to leave early.
mistake.right: My teacher let us leave early.
mistake.note: 'Let' is followed by an object and the base verb without 'to'.

senses.def: the amount, size or quality of something
ex: The noise level is very high.
What is your English level?

senses.def: the height of something in relation to the ground or sea
ex: The water level is rising.

senses.def: flat, with no part higher than the rest
ex: Find a level surface for the table.

senses.def: to make a surface flat
ex: Workers levelled the ground before building.

senses.def: to communicate with another person or group so that you can work well together
ex: She liaises with the police on safety issues.
We liaise closely with schools.

senses.def: communication and cooperation between people or groups
ex: There is close liaison between the two departments.
He acts as a liaison between staff and managers.

senses.def: a person who tells lies
ex: Nobody trusts him; he's a liar.
She called me a liar.

senses.def: accepting different opinions and ways of behaving, and not wanting strict rules
ex: She has liberal views on education.
He comes from a liberal family that welcomes debate.

senses.def: given or used in large amounts
ex: She added a liberal helping of cream.

senses.def: the act of making a person or place free from control or danger
ex: The liberation of the town took three days.
Many people celebrated the liberation of the prisoners.

senses.def: to give official permission for someone to do or sell something
ex: The government licenses restaurants to sell food.
The shop is licensed to sell alcohol.

mistake.wrong: I took a license for the car.
mistake.right: I got a licence for the car.
mistake.note: In British English the noun is spelt licence and the verb is spelt license.

senses.def: to move your tongue over something
ex: The dog licked my hand.
She licked the ice cream before it melted.

senses.def: a cover for the top of a pot, box or other container
ex: Put the lid back on the jar.
I can't find the lid for this pan.

senses.def: the piece of skin that covers your eye when you close it
ex: Her eyelids felt heavy.

senses.def: to be or put yourself flat on a surface
ex: He lay on the sofa and watched TV.
The book is lying on the table.

senses.def: to say something that you know is not true
ex: He lied about his age.

senses.def: something you say that you know is not true
ex: Don't tell lies to your parents.
It was a lie, and everyone knew it.

mistake.wrong: He lied to say he was sick.
mistake.right: He lied when he said he was sick.
mistake.note: Lie meaning to say something untrue is followed by to for the listener and about for the topic.

senses.def: the state of being alive, or the time between birth and death
ex: Life is full of surprises.
She spent her whole life in the same village.

senses.def: the way a person lives or the activities in their daily existence
ex: City life is very busy.
He has a quiet life in the country.

mistake.note: The plural of life is lives, not lifes.

senses.def: dead or seeming to be dead
ex: The lifeless body lay on the beach.
The soldier's lifeless hand dropped the flag.

senses.def: without energy, excitement or interest
ex: The singer gave a lifeless performance.

senses.def: the period of time during which someone is alive
ex: She wrote ten books in her lifetime.
Seeing the whale was a once-in-a-lifetime event.

senses.def: a machine that carries people up and down in a tall building
ex: Take the lift to the fifth floor.
The lift is out of order again.

senses.def: a free journey in someone's car
ex: Can I give you a lift to the station?

senses.def: to move something or someone up to a higher position
ex: He lifted the box onto the shelf.
She lifted her hand to wave.

senses.def: having a lot of natural light
ex: The room is light and airy.
It gets light early in the summer.

senses.def: not heavy, or not weighing much
ex: This bag is very light.
She wore a light jacket.

senses.def: the energy from the sun or a lamp that lets you see
ex: Turn on the light, please.
There wasn't enough light to read.

senses.def: to make something start to burn, or to make a place bright
ex: He lit a candle.
A single lamp lit the room.

senses.def: to become brighter, or to make something brighter
ex: The sky lightened as the sun rose.
She lightened her hair with a special spray.

senses.def: to make a situation or mood happier and less serious
ex: A joke helped to lighten the mood.

senses.def: a small device that makes a flame, used to light cigarettes or candles
ex: He took a lighter from his pocket.
I need a lighter for the candles.

senses.def: the type or arrangement of lights in a place
ex: The restaurant has soft lighting.
Good lighting is important in a studio.

senses.def: with very little force or weight
ex: She touched his arm lightly.
Snow fell lightly on the roofs.

senses.def: in a small amount
ex: Lightly salt the water.

senses.def: a bright flash of light in the sky during a storm
ex: The tree was hit by lightning.
We saw lightning and heard thunder.

mistake.note: Do not confuse lightning (the flash) with thunder (the sound).

senses.def: similar to someone or something
ex: She looks like her mother.
It sounds like a good idea.

senses.def: such as
ex: I enjoy sports like tennis and football.

senses.def: to find someone or something pleasant
ex: I like pizza.
Do you like swimming?

senses.def: used in would like to politely say what you want
ex: I would like a cup of tea.

senses.def: in the same way as; as if (informal)
ex: It looks like it's going to rain.

mistake.note: After like, use an -ing form or to + verb, not both together; also say I like it, not I like.

senses.def: how probable it is that something will happen
ex: There is a strong likelihood of rain tomorrow.
The likelihood of success is low.

senses.def: probable, or expected to happen or to be true
ex: It is likely to rain tonight.
He is likely to win the race.

mistake.wrong: It is likely that he will to come.
mistake.note: Use likely + to + base verb, or It is likely that + clause.

senses.def: in the same way, or also
ex: She voted for change, and her friends did likewise.
Treat others kindly and they will likewise treat you.

senses.def: an arm or a leg of a person or animal
ex: He broke a limb in the accident.
The patient lost the use of two limbs.

senses.def: a large branch of a tree
ex: A heavy limb fell from the oak.

senses.def: the greatest amount or level that is allowed or possible
ex: The speed limit here is 30 miles an hour.
There is a limit to what I can do.

senses.def: to stop something from going beyond a certain amount
ex: The school limits classes to twenty pupils.
Try to limit your sugar.

senses.def: small in number or amount
ex: We have limited time.
The shop has a limited choice of shoes.

senses.def: without any limit
ex: Children have a limitless imagination.
The desert seemed limitless.

senses.def: to walk with difficulty because one leg or foot is hurt
ex: The runner limped off the field.
He limped home with a sore ankle.

senses.def: a long thin mark on a surface
ex: Draw a straight line.
Write your name on the line.

senses.def: a row of people waiting for something
ex: There was a long line at the bank.

senses.def: to form a row along the edge of something
senses.ar: يصفّ على طول؛ يمتدّ على جانبي
ex: Trees line the road.
Crowds lined the streets to watch the parade.

senses.def: in a straight line, or involving a direct series of steps
ex: The graph shows a linear increase.
The story is not linear; it jumps through time.

senses.def: a cloth made from the plant flax, or sheets and cloths in a house
ex: She wore a white linen shirt.
The hotel changes the bed linen daily.

senses.def: a low shrub with small purple flowers that grows on moors
ex: Ling covered the hillside in late summer.
Sheep grazed among the ling and grass.

senses.def: to stay somewhere for longer than needed, or to last for a long time
ex: A few guests lingered after the party.
The smell of smoke lingered in the room.

senses.def: to continue to exist for a long time, often slowly
ex: Doubts lingered in his mind.

senses.def: a connection between two or more things or people
ex: There is a link between smoking and cancer.
The bridge is the only link to the island.

senses.def: a word or picture on a web page that you click to go to another page
ex: Click the link to read more.

senses.def: to connect two or more things or people
ex: A new road links the two cities.
The police linked him to the crime.

senses.def: in a form that flows, like water
ex: Melt the butter until it is liquid.

senses.def: a substance such as water or oil that flows and is not solid
ex: Mix the liquid with the flour.
Drink plenty of liquids.

senses.def: to pay attention to a sound
ex: Listen to this song.
She listens to the radio every morning.

senses.def: to follow someone's advice or instructions
ex: I told him, but he never listens.

mistake.note: Listen needs the preposition to before its object; hear does not.

senses.def: a person who listens, especially to the radio
ex: The radio asked listeners to send emails.
She is a very good listener.

senses.def: following the exact meaning of each word, not figurative
ex: The literal meaning of the word is "to carry across".
Don't take his joke in a literal way.

senses.def: in the exact meaning of the word, not as an exaggeration
ex: The word means "bookworm" literally.
He was literally the last person in the building.

senses.def: used to stress something, often as an exaggeration
ex: I literally died of laughter.

senses.def: connected with literature, or with writing as an art
ex: She won a famous literary prize.
He is interested in literary history.

senses.def: books, plays and poems that are valued as art
ex: She studies English literature at university.
He loved Arabic literature as a boy.

senses.def: printed information about a subject
ex: The clinic has literature on healthy eating.

senses.def: rubbish left lying on the ground in a public place
ex: Please do not drop litter.
The park was covered in litter.

senses.def: a group of baby animals born to one mother at the same time
ex: The cat had a litter of five kittens.

senses.def: small in size
ex: She has a little dog.
We live in a little town.

senses.def: not much; only a small amount
ex: I slept little last night.

senses.def: used with uncountable nouns to mean not much
ex: We have little time.

senses.def: a small amount
ex: I understood very little.

mistake.note: Use little with uncountable nouns (money) and few with plural countable nouns.

senses.def: to have your home in a place
ex: I live in Cairo.
They live near the sea.

senses.def: to be alive or to stay alive
ex: My grandfather lived to be ninety.

senses.def: seen or heard as it happens, not recorded
ex: We watched the live match on TV.
The band plays live music on Fridays.

mistake.note: Do not use the before the name of a city.

senses.def: a large organ in the body that cleans the blood
ex: The liver helps to remove poison from the body.
Too much alcohol can damage your liver.

senses.def: alive now
ex: Are your grandparents still living?
He is the oldest living person in the town.

senses.def: the money someone earns from their work
ex: What do you do for a living?
She earns a living as a taxi driver.

senses.def: something heavy that is carried
ex: The truck carried a heavy load.
The donkey was tired from its load.

senses.def: to put things onto or into a vehicle, machine or computer
ex: They loaded the boxes into the van.
Please load the software before you start.

senses.def: bread baked in one piece that you cut into slices
ex: Buy a loaf of bread.
The loaf was still warm from the oven.

senses.def: an amount of money that you borrow, usually from a bank
ex: He took out a loan to buy a house.
The bank refused her a loan.

senses.def: something given to be used for a short time
ex: The painting is on loan to a museum.

senses.def: a large area just inside the entrance of a building
ex: We waited in the hotel lobby.
The lobby of the theatre was crowded.

senses.def: a group of people who try to influence politicians
ex: The farmers' lobby opposes the new law.

senses.def: connected with the area where you live or a particular area
ex: I bought the bread at a local shop.
The local news is on at six.

senses.def: to find the exact position of someone or something
ex: Police are trying to locate the missing boy.
Can you locate the village on the map?

senses.def: to put or build something in a certain place
ex: They located the factory near the port.

senses.def: the place where someone or something is
ex: The hotel is in a great location.
Please send me your exact location.

senses.def: a device that keeps a door, box or window shut
ex: I can't open the lock.
He changed the locks on the doors.

senses.def: to close something with a key or similar device
ex: Lock the door when you leave.
The window will not lock.

senses.def: the engine at the front of a train that pulls it
ex: The locomotive pulled twenty carriages.
An old steam locomotive stood in the station.

senses.def: a small house or hut, often used by hunters or skiers
ex: We stayed in a ski lodge in the mountains.
The porter's lodge is by the gate.

senses.def: to officially present a complaint or request
ex: He lodged a complaint with the council.

senses.def: to pay to live in someone's house for a time
ex: She lodged with an elderly couple.

senses.def: a thick piece of wood cut from a tree
ex: He put another log on the fire.
They sat on a fallen log.

senses.def: a written record of events, especially on a ship or computer
ex: The captain wrote the event in the ship's log.

senses.def: a way of thinking in which each step follows from the one before
ex: There is no logic in his argument.
I don't follow the logic of that decision.

senses.def: to stay in a place without any clear reason
ex: Teenagers were loitering outside the shop.
Please do not loiter near the entrance.

senses.def: the sad feeling of being alone and wanting company
ex: Many old people suffer from loneliness.
He felt a deep loneliness after moving abroad.

senses.def: measuring a great distance from one end to the other
ex: She has long dark hair.
It's a long road to the village.

senses.def: lasting a lot of time
ex: It was a long meeting.

senses.def: for a large amount of time
ex: I didn't wait long.
How long have you lived here?

senses.def: travelling or communicating between places that are far apart
ex: He is a long-distance runner.
We had a long-distance relationship for two years.

senses.def: made between two places that are far apart
ex: She makes long-distance calls to her sister every week.

senses.def: continuing for a long time into the future
ex: We need a long-term plan.
He has a long-term illness.

senses.def: an act of directing your eyes at something
ex: Take a look at this photo.
She gave me a strange look.

senses.def: the way a person or thing seems
ex: I like the look of this house.

senses.def: to direct your eyes towards someone or something
ex: Look at the board.
She looked out of the window.

senses.def: to seem or appear
ex: You look tired.
That cake looks delicious.

mistake.note: Look needs at before the thing you are looking at.

senses.def: to take care of someone or something
ex: She looks after her younger brother.
Can you look after my cat while I'm away?

mistake.wrong: I look after my keys but I can't find them.
mistake.right: I'm looking for my keys but I can't find them.
mistake.note: look after = يعتني. look for = يبحث عن.

senses.def: to appear as a large, often frightening shape
ex: A tall building loomed out of the mist.
Dark clouds loomed over the hills.

senses.def: to seem about to happen, in a worrying way
ex: Exams are looming and I haven't studied.

senses.def: not tight, or not fixed firmly in place
ex: He wore loose trousers.
One of the screws is loose.

senses.def: not held or fastened; free
ex: The dog was loose in the garden.

mistake.wrong: Please do not lose the door.
mistake.right: Please do not leave the door loose.
mistake.note: Do not confuse loose (adjective) with lose (verb).

senses.def: to no longer have something because you cannot find it
ex: I lost my keys.
She lost her job last year.

senses.def: to fail to win a game or competition
ex: Our team lost the match.
He lost the election.

senses.def: the fact of no longer having something, or the state of losing
ex: The loss of her job was a shock.
He felt grief at the loss of his friend.

senses.def: the money that a business loses
ex: The company made a loss this year.

senses.def: not knowing where you are or how to go somewhere
ex: I'm lost; can you help me?
A lost child was crying in the street.

senses.def: that cannot be found
ex: I'm looking for my lost keys.

senses.def: very much or very often (a lot)
ex: Thank you very much; I like it a lot.
It rains a lot here.

senses.def: a large number or amount (a lot of)
ex: She has lots to do.

senses.def: a large amount or number
ex: There are a lot of people in the park.
We have lots of time.

mistake.note: Use a lot of before a noun and a lot alone at the end of a clause.

senses.def: a game in which people buy numbered tickets and win money if their number is chosen
ex: She won the lottery.
He buys a lottery ticket every week.

senses.def: making a lot of noise
ex: The music was too loud.
He has a loud voice.

senses.def: at a high volume
ex: Please don't talk so loud.

senses.def: very bad in quality (informal)
ex: The food was lousy.
I had a lousy day at work.

senses.def: a strong feeling of caring for someone or liking something very much
ex: Their love for each other is clear.
She has a love of music.

senses.def: to have strong feelings of caring for someone
ex: I love my family.
They love each other.

senses.def: to like something very much
ex: She loves chocolate.
He loves playing football.

senses.def: a person in a romantic relationship with someone
ex: Romeo was Juliet's lover.
She took a lover.

senses.def: a person who enjoys a particular thing very much
ex: He is a music lover.
The café is popular with book lovers.

senses.def: not high or tall; near the ground
ex: The ceiling is very low.
He sat on a low chair.

senses.def: small in amount, level or value
ex: Prices are low in the market.
The soup is low in fat.

senses.def: in or to a low position
ex: The plane flew low over the town.

senses.def: to reduce the level or amount of something
ex: The bank lowered its interest rate.
Please lower your voice.

senses.def: to move something down slowly
ex: They lowered the flag at sunset.

senses.def: always supporting a person, group or idea
ex: He is a loyal friend.
Loyal fans stayed until the end of the game.

senses.def: the quality of being loyal
ex: Dogs are known for their loyalty.
The company rewards customer loyalty.

senses.def: good or bad things that happen to you by chance
ex: Good luck with your exam!
It was just luck that I found it.

mistake.wrong: I wish you a good luck.
mistake.note: Luck is uncountable, so it has no a or plural.

senses.def: producing a lot of money
ex: He got a lucrative job in banking.
The company signed a lucrative contract.

senses.def: so silly or unreasonable that it makes people laugh
ex: It's ludicrous to pay that much for a T-shirt.
The idea sounded ludicrous at first.

senses.def: the bags and cases you take on a journey
ex: I left my luggage at the airport.
How much luggage can I carry?

mistake.right: I have three bags of luggage.
mistake.note: Luggage is uncountable, so it has no plural; use a piece of luggage.

senses.def: one of the two organs in your chest that you use for breathing
ex: Smoking can damage the lungs.
He took a deep breath and filled his lungs.

senses.def: shocking, especially because of unpleasant details
ex: The newspaper printed lurid details of the crime.
He told a lurid story.

senses.def: unpleasantly bright in colour
ex: She wore a lurid pink dress.

senses.def: growing thickly and healthily
ex: The valley is lush and green.
Rain fell on the lush gardens.

senses.def: rich and comfortable
ex: The hotel has a lush bar and spa.

senses.def: a very strong wish for something, especially power or money
ex: His lust for power ruined him.
She had a lust for adventure.

senses.def: very comfortable and expensive
ex: They stayed at a luxurious hotel.
She lives in a luxurious flat.

senses.def: great comfort, especially from expensive things
ex: They live in luxury.
A holiday is a luxury for many families.

senses.def: of a high quality and price
ex: They stayed in a luxury hotel.
She drives a luxury car.

senses.def: expressing strong feelings in a beautiful, poetic way
ex: She gave a lyrical description of the countryside.
His lyrical prose is easy to remember.

senses.def: the words of a song
ex: I know all the lyrics of this song.
He writes lyrics for famous singers.
